spans.s: śaya (IE 3-4), derived from a Chinese word; paper.

sāyana (CII 3), ‘inclusive of precession^1 of the equinoxes’.
[1] Correction submitted by Dr. Sampada Savardekar on 20210207. Reference: https://github.com/sanskrit-lexicon/csl-corrections/issues/51.
śayanīya, a cot; cf. śayanīy-āsana-siddānnaṃ na dāpayet (Ep. Ind., Vol. XXX, p. 171).
sāyara (PJS), Arabic shāher; a tax on palm-tree juice.
Śayyāgrāhaka (HD), explained as ‘the guardian of the bed-chamber.’ See A. S. Gadre, Imp. Ins. Bar. St., p. 72. Cf. Śayyāpāla, Vāsāgārika, Vitān-ādhipa.
Śayyāpāla (EI 25; HD), officer in charge of the king's bed [] (i. e. bed-chamber); guardian of the bed-chamber. See Śayyāgrāhaka, Vāsāgārika, Vitān-ādhipa.
